# Draft:JD Vance 2028 presidential campaign

JD Vance, the 50th vice president of the United States, is widely expected to announce his candidacy for the 2028 United States presidential election.
Pre-candidacy developments
]]
In December 2023, Politico Magazines Bill Scher argued that Vance was positioned to continue Trumpism for his association with Donald Trump, particularly Trump's alleged authoritarianism; Scher additionally noted Vance's willingness to work with Democrats on bills relating to rail safety, executive compensation, and foreign technology. As Trump began considering choices for a vice presidential candidate, the choice was believed to affect the expected front-runner in the 2028 Republican Party presidential primaries; according to Bloomberg News prior to Trump's final choice, Vance's selection would allow him to become the "standard-bearer of Trumpism" and a "favorite for the Republican presidential nomination". After Trump named Vance as his running mate, Vance was believed to have become the "heir apparent" for the Republican Party, according to The Hill and USA Today.
South Dakota senator John Thune argued that Vance leading the Republican Party would be dependent on the success of his vice presidency, should he be elected, while Jeff Kaufmann, the chair of the Republican Party of Iowa, anticipated he would be a front-runner if he were elected vice president, but added that a "robust caucus" would exist for the 2028 presidential election. The Times considered Vance as a possible "Trumpian president" for the 2028 election. According to ABC News, Vance was among several potential candidates being considered for the 2028 presidential election, including former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley and Florida governor Ron DeSantis, though the Republican strategist Michael DuHaime stated that Vance's selection strengthened his standing relative to Haley and DeSantis. The New York Timess Nate Cohn considered Vance a "top-tier presidential contender in 2028".
Following the vice presidential debate in October 2024, Politico Magazine and The Columbus Dispatch considered Vance's debate performance as influential in the 2028 presidential election. In December, Utah senator Mitt Romney, the Republican nominee in the 2012 presidential election, predicted Vance would be the nominee in 2028. In February 2025, Vance declined to answer a question from Fox News's Maria Bartiromo on if he was running for president in 2028. In a Fox News interview the following week, Trump said he did not consider Vance as his successor; Vance concurred in Trump's assessment that it was "too early" to consider a successor.
In March 2025, Axios reported that many of Trump's allies, including Indiana senator Jim Banks, considered Vance as the "vehicle to lock in Trump's worldview", noting his speech at the Munich Security Conference and his appearance at Trump's meeting with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The alt-right political activist Jack Posobiec repeatedly referred to Vance as "forty-eight", referencing becoming the forty-eighth president in 2028. Vance's vice presidency reportedly impressed Donald Trump Jr., who encouraged Trump to select Vance as his running mate. Axioss report was corroborated by Semafor, which reserved that his lack of experience concerned some in the Trump administration. Montana senator Steve Daines told Semafor that Vance was the likely nominee for 2028. The Wall Street Journal additionally reported that the political activist Scott Presler had already started a campaign in Pennsylvania to help Vance win the state in 2028. After Vance was named as the finance chair of the Republican National Committee that month, The New York Times and Axios associated the move to possibly building a fundraising network.
In May, Trump rejected an unconstitutional third term and considered secretary of state Marco Rubio and Vance as possible successors. Trump's comments stoked a competition between the men, though they were not reportedly in conflict, according to Semafor. In a Fox News interview, Vance rejected claims of a rivalry. While Rubio and Vance were present for the inauguration of Pope Leo XIV in the Vatican City, Vance told NBC News that he was not entitled to a presidential campaign in 2028. Vance's appearance at the American Compass's The New World Gala was believed to further establish his potential 2028 candidacy, including Politico. As Vance promoted the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, several Democrats believed to be considering presidential campaigns, including California governor Gavin Newsom and New York representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, sought to portray him as the central figure behind its passage. In August, Trump stated that Vance was "probably favored at this point" for the 2028 election; Vance told Fox News that it was "way too early" to consider a bid.
Financials
In September 2025, NBC News reported that Trump's fundraising emails contained links to direct donations that sent five percent of proceeds to Vance's political action committee, Working for Ohio. Beginning in February 2026, several aides to Vance began leaving for lobbying firms, including Sean J. Cooksey, his counsel; Jim Durrett, his deputy chief of staff for operations; and Wesam Hassanein, his Middle East advisor.
Polling and endorsements
At the 2025 Conservative Political Action Conference, Vance won a straw poll of attendees with sixty-one percent of respondents stating they would vote for him in 2028. Jim McLaughlin, who conducted the survey, told Axios that Vance won because he was "viewed as the closest thing to Donald Trump". Vance continued to lead in a McLaughlin & Associates poll that month, a poll between The Economist and YouGov in April, a JL Partners poll and an Emerson College poll in May, and a poll between YouGov and Yahoo in September.
In February 2025, Marco Rubio told Vanity Fair—in an interview published in December—that he would support Vance's campaign. Rubio repeated his comments in July. Erika Kirk, the widow of the political activist Charlie Kirk and the heir of Turning Point USA, endorsed Vance for president in December and vowed to support his campaign. In January 2026, Virginia governor Glenn Youngkin said that Vance would be a "great nominee".
